newsitem.title: CHINA: China tells Christians to toe Communist Party line.
newsitem.headline: China tells Christians to toe Communist Party line.

text.p: A senior Chinese official on Friday commended the nation's Christians for holding high the banner of socialism and urged them to continue to toe the Communist Party line.
Li Ruihuan, a member of the party's powerful Politburo, had urged Christians and other religious groups to comply with the party's religious policies, the Xinhua news agency said.
"Li expressed the hope that Chinese religious groups can have a good understanding of the religious policies of the party and the state and can put them into effect," Xinhua said.
Li had made the remarks at a national Christian conference meeting in Beijing, the agency said.
China's Christians should heed the slogan "a good Christian should be a good citizen" so as to make greater contributions to the country's ethical and cultural progress, it quoted Li as saying.

"Remarkable progress has been made by the Chinese Christians over the past 40 or more years...in being actively involved in socialist modernisation by holding the patriotic and socialist banner high," Li said.
China condones Christian worship only under the auspices of officially santioned, state-controlled churches and views underground congregations as a threat to party rule.
China's official Protestant association claimed about eight million members in 1994, while those worshippers in underground churches were estimated to number 20 million.
